title: Experiment: the application reader under a production build
summary: The reader was exercised from a temporary Server Component route under `next build` + `next start`. The route built as `ƒ /probe-read` — DYNAMIC — while `/`, which reads nothing, stayed `○` static. All three reads returned live project data: nine stages with `currentStage` null (every gate ready), 236 artifacts, 0 lint findings, 36 assertions; `06-risk-feasibility` ready with two criteria, the first `high-severity-risks-mitigated` satisfied; and the stage document read back as `06-risk-feasibility.md`, 10590 bytes. The probe route was deleted and the tree rebuilt clean.

omissions.reason: The reads are separate exports, which is the SHAPE independent boundaries require, but no view puts them behind boundaries yet — the stage view is TSK-0009. ACC-0016 therefore stays not-evaluated: the thing it measures does not exist.
The route was measured as dynamic, not measured serving changed content after a write while running. That is what the route symbol predicts and it was not confirmed here.

notes: ⚠️ `ƒ` IS THE OBSERVABLE THAT MATTERS, and it is the contract showing up in the build output: `connection()` made the route dynamic, so nothing it reads can be baked into the build. `/` staying `○` in the same build is the control — the difference is the contract, not the project.
